description: Built-in offline question bank for llm-benchmark. Deterministic, programmatically-graded questions across nine categories, including forward-development coding (Python, C, C++) and a vulnerability-research / reverse-engineering core set.

There are three boxes: one has only apples, one has only oranges, one has both. All three labels are wrong. You pick one fruit from the box labeled "Apples and Oranges" and get an apple. Is that box actually the apples-only box? Answer yes or no only.
In a race, Alice finishes before Bob, and Bob finishes before Carol. Does Alice finish before Carol? Answer yes or no only.
A statement says "This statement is false." Can this statement be consistently assigned a true or false value? Answer yes or no only.

A farmer has 17 sheep, and all but 9 die. How many sheep are left? Respond with only the number.

You have two ropes; each takes exactly 60 minutes to burn end-to-end but burns unevenly along its length. Using only these two ropes and matches, is it possible to measure exactly 45 minutes? Answer yes or no only.
If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, how many minutes would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets? Respond with only the number.

The 32-bit integer 0x41424344 is stored at some address on a little-endian x86-64 machine. List its four bytes in order of increasing memory address, as space-separated two-digit hex values (for example: aa bb cc dd).
Interpreted as a signed 8-bit two's-complement integer, what decimal value does the byte 0xFF represent? Respond with only the number.

What CPU/OS memory-protection feature marks the stack (and other data pages) as non-executable so injected shellcode cannot run from them? Answer with the common two- or three-letter acronym (as used on x86/Windows).
What exploit-mitigation technique randomizes the base addresses of the stack, heap, and shared libraries at load time so hardcoded addresses become unreliable? Answer with the acronym only.

A stack ______ is a known guard value the compiler places just before the saved return address; if it has been altered when the function returns, the program aborts instead of returning. Fill in the single missing word.
Which x86-64 instruction mnemonic pops the return address off the stack into RIP to return from a function? Answer with just the mnemonic.
In an ELF executable, which standard section normally holds the program's executable machine-code instructions? Answer with the section name including its leading dot.

Chaining together short instruction sequences that already exist in a binary and each end in a `ret` (called gadgets), in order to bypass a non-executable stack, is known by what three-letter acronym?

In C's printf family, which conversion specifier writes the number of characters output so far into the integer pointed to by its argument, making it the key write primitive in format-string exploits? Answer with the specifier including its percent sign.

Name the classic memory-corruption vulnerability class in which writing more data than a fixed-size stack buffer can hold overwrites adjacent memory such as the saved return address. Answer with the two- or three-word name for it.
Which GNU binutils command-line tool disassembles object files and executables, for example when invoked as `______ -d ./a.out`? Answer with just the tool name.

Name the free, open-source software reverse-engineering suite, featuring an interactive decompiler, that was developed and publicly released by the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA). Answer with the tool's name only.
